decisions.note: Round 2 plan gate: maker offered backend(auto-title) vs browser-only(manual-title) alternative; client selected the backend option, preserving auto-metadata capture.

Round 1 spec said duplicate URLs merely 'warn' (not guide-to-edit); client approved 'the rest' without probing; later plan softened to a 409/offer-update flow but this was maker-initiated, never client-confirmed.
Unread/read-later marking and a separate unread view were never surfaced across spec/plan/tasks/build; client never asked for it (no extend).
Multi-select bulk actions and 'apply to whole filtered collection' never appear in any round; client affirmed the full build without requesting them.
Only 'recent-first ordering' was delivered (round 4); a user-selectable sort key (title, date, etc.) was never presented or requested.
Tag-entry autocomplete against existing tags is absent from spec, plan, and final recap; not raised by client.
Search was scoped to plain 'title/address/tags' matching only; #tag syntax, AND/OR/NOT+parens, and quoted-phrase exact match never appear; client approved without extending scope.
No note/markdown field was ever introduced in the entity model or UI; client never asked for it.
No local HTML/PDF snapshot or Internet Archive snapshot capability was proposed or built; passed over silently.
Delivered soft-delete+undo-window only; no persistent, reversible archive state or separate archive view distinct from delete was ever presented.
Bundles (saved search-term + tag-filter combinations) never appear in any artifact; not requested by client.

Round 1 spec explicitly states 'Browser import/export deferred to a later iteration' as a flagged assumption; client's 'the rest looks good... go ahead' affirmed this diverging deferral without contesting it — a clear-cut satisficing miss.
Personal display settings (default sort, items-per-page, font size) were never mentioned in spec, plan, or build; not requested.

Only title auto-derivation was confirmed (round 2 backend discussion); description/favicon/preview-image auto-collection and their display in the list were never explicitly presented or confirmed as built.
